title: Jain Pilgrimage in India: Tirthas, Temples and How to Visit
seoTitle: Jain Pilgrimage in India: Tirthas & How to Visit | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: A guide to Jain pilgrimage in India: Palitana, Sammed Shikharji, Ranakpur, Dilwara, Shravanabelagola, Girnar and Pawapuri, with climbs, etiquette and festivals.
description: A guide to Jain tirthas in India: Shatrunjaya at Palitana and Sammed Shikharji, the two holiest hills, the marble temples of Ranakpur and Dilwara, Shravanabelagola's Gommateshwara, Girnar, Pawapuri and Sonagiri, with climbs, visiting rules, festivals such as Paryushan and suggested routes.
dek: Jain tirthas range from hilltop temple cities climbed at dawn to some of the finest marble carving in India.

hero.alt: Jain temples crowning Shatrunjaya hill at Palitana, Gujarat

intro: A tirtha, meaning a ford or crossing place, is a sacred site in Jainism, usually linked with the lives of the twenty-four Tirthankaras. Many are hills covered with temples, climbed on foot at dawn; others are richly carved temples in towns and forests.

Shatrunjaya at Palitana (Gujarat) and Sammed Shikharji (Jharkhand) are regarded by many Jains as the holiest. Both Svetambara and Digambara traditions have their own important tirthas, and visitors of all backgrounds are welcome at most temples if they follow the rules.
quickAnswer: The most important Jain pilgrimage sites in India include Shatrunjaya hill at Palitana (Gujarat), with about 863 temples reached by some 3,500 steps; Sammed Shikharji on Parasnath hill (Jharkhand), where 20 of the 24 Tirthankaras are believed to have attained moksha; the marble temples of Ranakpur and Dilwara (Rajasthan); Shravanabelagola (Karnataka); Girnar (Gujarat); and Pawapuri (Bihar). October to March is the best season.
takeaways: Palitana and Sammed Shikharji are regarded by many Jains as the holiest sites.
Hill tirthas are climbed early in the morning, and descending before evening is customary.
Ranakpur and Dilwara are among India's finest marble temples.
Leather and food are usually not allowed inside Jain temples.
October to March is best; climbs in summer heat are hard.

items.name: Shatrunjaya, Palitana
body: The climb of roughly 3,500 steps starts before dawn; the temple city on top is closed at night, and pilgrims descend the same day. Dolis (carried chairs) are available.

image.alt: Temples on Shatrunjaya hill at Palitana, Gujarat
image.caption: Palitana, Gujarat

items.name: Sammed Shikharji
body: Pilgrims walk a long circuit of Parasnath hill from Madhuban, visiting the shrines (tonks) of the Tirthankaras. Most start around midnight or very early morning to finish in a day.

items.name: Girnar
body: Temples of Neminath and other shrines rise above Junagadh; a ropeway now reaches part of the way up.

items.name: Ranakpur
body: A four-faced (chaumukha) temple to Adinath, built in the 15th century, traditionally said to have 1,444 carved pillars, no two alike.

items.name: Dilwara
body: A group of temples at Mount Abu, including Vimal Vasahi and Luna Vasahi, famous for delicate marble ceilings. Photography is not allowed inside.

sections.heading: Other important sites
list: Shravanabelagola, Karnataka: Bahubali's statue on Vindhyagiri and the basadis of Chandragiri.
Pawapuri, Bihar: the Jal Mandir in a lotus pond, marking Mahavira's nirvana.
Rajgir and Kundalpur, Bihar: sites linked with Mahavira's life.
Sonagiri, Madhya Pradesh: a hill of Digambar temples near Datia.
Shri Mahavirji, Rajasthan: a major pilgrimage temple in Karauli district.
after: Traditions sometimes differ on the exact places linked with events in Mahavira's life; the list follows common pilgrim practice.

sections.heading: Festivals
list: Paryushan (August or September), the most important period of fasting and reflection.
Diwali, which Jains mark as Mahavira's nirvana.
Kartik Purnima, when large numbers climb Shatrunjaya after the monsoon.
The Mahamastakabhisheka at Shravanabelagola, held every 12 years; the next is due in 2030.

safety: Jain temples usually ask visitors not to carry leather or food inside, to dress modestly and to follow posted rules; some set separate visiting hours for non-Jain visitors.
Start hill climbs early, carry water and avoid the midday heat.
Dolis are available at Palitana and Girnar for those who cannot climb; agree rates at the official counters.
Follow the rule of descending hill tirthas before evening.
packing: Water and a hat for climbs
Socks for hot stone steps where footwear is removed

faqs.q: Which is the holiest Jain pilgrimage site?
faqs.a: Many Jains regard Shatrunjaya at Palitana and Sammed Shikharji in Jharkhand as the holiest.

faqs.q: How many steps are there at Palitana?
faqs.a: About 3,500 steps to the temple city on Shatrunjaya hill.
Yes, at most temples, though some set separate visiting hours and all have rules on leather, food and dress.

faqs.q: When is the best time for Jain pilgrimage?
faqs.a: October to March. Kartik Purnima marks the reopening of Shatrunjaya climbs after the monsoon.
